I would give implementation and interactive acceptance to different agents in clean, separate Codex tasks. Interactive UI and a possible defect/retest cycle require a durable walkthrough lane; a deterministic same-task verifier is insufficient. I would reconcile the current project brief, decisions, feature and walkthrough, record pwd/status/HEAD, preserve dirty work, and establish the Git delivery contract before any feature write. I would reconcile docs/project/active-lanes.json and validate it with python3 scripts/validate_coordination_contracts.py lanes docs/project/active-lanes.json before admitting independent lanes. A sequential walkthrough of this same feature does not become a second unrelated feature track.

Before dispatch I would resolve current role-card and packet paths and fill each worker prompt with Role; Reasoning profile; Profile trigger and risk floor; exact Agent preset/model/effort; Access posture; Escalation conditions; Goal; Success criteria; Required evidence and source authority; Scope and allowed files; Human and permission boundaries; Validation required; Output packet; Stop and fallback rules; Execution mode: separate task; Assigned return destination; and Read first. Its separate-task fields would name the exact task title, coordinator identity, worker id when known, worktree, branch/commit and final packet. The implementation assignment would additionally state separate-worktree or proven disjoint sharing, owned files and Do not edit. I would select Balanced Terra/medium for a settled reversible implementation unless actual risk signals raise its floor; the walkthrough's manual judgment warrants Deep Astra/high with access limited to necessary verification. I would verify effective settings and never silently downgrade an unavailable preset. No parallel A/B extension is needed for this single feature.

Implementation owns only its declared feature worktree/files, preserves the active spec and walkthrough, runs focused checks, and commits only under branch+commit authority. It returns one implementation packet in its own task, naming changed files, exact commit, checks/gaps, risks, retest focus and remaining closeout, then stops. It never accepts or integrates its own work. I would perform one bounded start-health check, collect the final packet with wait/read tools, confirm receipt and check ownership and clean committed state.

The walkthrough task would inspect that exact commit against approved acceptance criteria and the current walkthrough, perform the authorized UI scenarios and return readiness or reproducible defect evidence in its own task. Accounts, secrets, setup or external changes remain human gates, not implied permission. Defects return to the implementation owner; new commits require affected retests by the walkthrough owner. I would collect both packets without requiring cross-task sends. Passing acceptance produces Merge-ready, not Delivered. I retain coordinator ownership of integration, required checks, bookkeeping and authorized cleanup; missing external authority leaves Ready for Git closeout. A missing source, mismatched checkout, overlapping owner or unmet gate stops the affected lane with a blocker.

I would admit two independent workstreams as separate clean Codex tasks, tracks A and B, after verifying the stated isolation against current sources. Each has its own implementation owner and independently testable acceptance outcome. First I would record the Git baseline and reconcile docs/project/active-lanes.json from current owning packets and actual checkout evidence. The record uses schemaVersion:1, contractKind:active-lanes, updatedAt and lanes whose entries contain id, owner, task, status, worktree, branchOrCommit, currentPacket and recoveryOwner. Active, blocked and parked rows all consume slots; complete/superseded rows remain history. I would run python3 scripts/validate_coordination_contracts.py lanes docs/project/active-lanes.json and stop admission if the inventory is unresolved or the cap would be exceeded.

For each feature I would declare the delivery contract before writes: Base branch; Feature branch; Worktree; Delivery mode; any direct-to-base rationale/approval; Integration path; Merge method; Remote and base target; Local Git authority; External Git authority; Remote branch cleanup; Closeout owner: coordinator. Concurrent writers would normally get separate worktrees and branches from the same accepted common base. I would verify no independent writes to the same schema, migration sequence, API contract, lockfile, generated source, global configuration, shared fixture or external environment. Roadmap and decision log stay coordinator-owned. If any shared boundary appears, serialize or ask the architect to resolve that boundary before launch.

Both prompts would fill the complete core worker contract: role, selected profile/risk floor, exact access-specific preset/model/effort, access posture, escalation conditions, goal, criteria, authority/evidence, owned scope/files, human gates, validation, packet, stop/fallback, execution mode, return destination and resolved Read first. Separate-task extensions name title, coordinator, task id if known, worktree, branch/commit and final packet. Write extensions state sharing and exclusions. Each prompt also records Parallel track:A or B, Common base commit, Integration target, Expected worktree, Expected branch, Allowed files/surfaces, Shared surfaces excluded, Cross-track assumptions, Integration order and Combined checks. Concrete values must come from the accepted specs and current state rather than guessed names or commands. I would verify effective model/effort and one bounded start-health receipt for each task.

Workers return a single track-tagged final packet in their own tasks; I collect via wait/read and confirm receipt without polling active workers or requiring messages. Independent acceptance stays separate from implementation wherever required. A blocker in one track does not stop the other unless a shared assumption changes. Each individually accepted result is Track-ready. I would restate the authoritative architecture and evidence limits for integration, integrate in the declared order, inspect conflicts/changed assumptions, run named combined checks and repeat affected walkthrough scenarios. Only then is the combined state Integration-verified. I would report each track and the combined result separately, complete authorized Git closeout and reconcile lane/roadmap records. Changed scope, conflicts, failed checks or changed Git targets return to the relevant owner or human gate; neither track's isolated pass authorizes delivery of the combined state.

I would queue the third feature and leave its implementation unstarted. Two nonterminal admitted tracks already occupy A and B; another task, subagent or parked label cannot bypass that cap.

I would reconcile docs/project/active-lanes.json against current owning packets and checkout evidence, recording schemaVersion:1, contractKind:active-lanes, updatedAt and each lane's id, owner, task, status, worktree, branchOrCommit, currentPacket and recoveryOwner. Active, blocked and parked entries remain unresolved and occupy slots; complete and superseded entries remain history. I would run python3 scripts/validate_coordination_contracts.py lanes docs/project/active-lanes.json. Idle chat state, a clean worktree or a remembered handoff does not prove a lane terminal. I would collect any already-returned final packet and reconcile its actual completion before claiming a free slot.

Read-only preparation of the third feature may proceed in the coordinator: settle its brief, acceptance, isolated ownership, delivery choices and dependency assumptions, record it as queued in project state, and name the next owner. I would not create a third unresolved independent lane or dispatch an implementation subagent. If the human changes priority, I would arrange explicit safe completion or supersession of an existing lane, preserving unfinished work, evidence and recovery ownership; merely blocking or parking it does not release admission capacity.

When at most one unresolved track remains, I would revalidate the inventory and the third feature's current assumptions, then use the full two-track admission and Git delivery contracts before dispatch. Until that event the result is Third feature queued; existing tracks retain their owners and authority, with coordinator-owned next action: collect an existing terminal result or resolve a safe supersession. No cleanup, branch deletion, external write or acceptance is implied.

I would not launch another independent workstream: the active lane and the parked lane both occupy admission slots. Parking preserves an unresolved ownership/recovery obligation; it is not completion.

I would verify the current docs/project/active-lanes.json and its named owning packets against current sources. Its envelope is schemaVersion:1, contractKind:active-lanes, updatedAt; each row keeps id, owner, task, status, worktree, branchOrCommit, currentPacket and recoveryOwner. I would retain both rows with truthful active/parked statuses, identify the parked work's remaining outcome and recovery owner, and run python3 scripts/validate_coordination_contracts.py lanes docs/project/active-lanes.json. Missing evidence or conflicting identities blocks admission, rather than permitting removal of a row. Old summaries, idle chats and clean checkouts cannot close a lane.

I would keep the new work in the coordinator's queue with a bounded proposed scope and acceptance plan. To free a slot, the relevant owning lane must actually complete, or be explicitly superseded with unfinished work and recovery preserved; those terminal rows stay as history. I would not restart the parked task, send it a message or discard its work merely to make the ledger fit. Any needed human reprioritization or destructive/external action remains a separate decision. Once a terminal packet is collected and recorded, I would reconcile and validate the ledger again and then reassess independence, ownership, common base, integration order, combined checks and Git authority before admitting the next track. The current operational state is admission blocked by two unresolved lanes, with recovery and queue ownership explicit.

I would proceed from the accepted bounded brief without adding an architect pass. Explicit acceptance, file ownership and validation plus settled decisions satisfy the skip criteria; no unresolved architecture trigger exists. I would first verify pwd, git status --short --branch and git rev-parse HEAD and confirm the named scope against current sources, preserving any unexpected dirty paths.

Before writes I would establish the proportionate Git delivery contract. Product code requires a feature branch even for a small change. The normal contract records base/feature branch, current or separate worktree, delivery mode and exception approval if any, integration path, merge method, remote/base target, local authority, external authority, remote cleanup and coordinator closeout owner. If this is instead one reversible process/admin-only surface and every micro-slice criterion passes, current status may record scope, exact state, owner, focused deterministic check, evidence, explicit rollback and stop boundary; a direct-to-base exception still needs explicit human approval. A one-owner change alone does not prove the micro-slice criteria.

I would keep the work in the same task or use one bounded implementation subagent only if all subagent conditions pass: one return, no direct human/external requirement, no independent recovery lane, current worktree, disjoint ownership and immediate parent inspection. A subagent prompt would name the parent and return destination, Subagents:not allowed, owned files, worktree, changed-file report, full core assignment, canonical implementation card/packet and Balanced Terra/medium workspace-write unless new risks raise the floor. A durable task is used only if an actual separate-task trigger appears. No independent parallel-track fields are needed.

The implementation owner makes only the allowed edit, runs the specified meaningful checks, returns exact changed files and state, and commits only when granted branch+commit. The parent inspects the result and owns the final quality gate. Product behavior receives independent acceptance by a different agent as required; a qualifying deterministic micro-slice may use the parent-run focused check and one receipt. A new shared contract, disputed source, overlap, unresolved requirement or failed oracle stops the slice for rerouting, not silent scope expansion. I would reconcile project status and finish the authorized Git lifecycle; working-tree-only work is not Merge-ready, an accepted committed feature is Merge-ready until integration, and Delivered requires verified integration, checks and contract-matching cleanup.

I would perform a read-only project-evolution audit and render the packet in the response; I would not apply recommendations or create a report file. I would record project and template branch/HEAD/dirty state, recorded template and last-sync commits and baseline confidence, run the current template's scripts/audit_mamkin_evolution.py inventory according to its documented interface, and inspect only plausible candidates' current brief, decisions, lessons, follow-ups, actual usage, checks, hooks, skills and relevant history. Initial and final Git status would show whether the audit preserved the worktree. A dirty template can inform capability assessment but cannot serve as an executable sync source.

Each capability would be classified Upgrade gap, Project leverage, Redundancy or No-fit. Absence upstream is insufficient evidence. The gate is two concrete recurring occurrences, one high-impact safety/recovery/ownership gap, a missing deterministic prerequisite in a repeatedly updated/customized project, or a measured regression the mechanic addresses. Repeated sync customization makes a deterministic prerequisite worth investigating, but I would cite actual artifacts/occurrences and avoid inventing scores or commands. The inventory identifies candidates; it does not establish usefulness.

For each evidence-backed candidate I would score Benefit = recurrence(0–3)+time/token saving(0–3)+risk reduction(0–3)+project fit/confidence(0–2); Cost = adoption effort(0–3)+maintenance(0–3); Net=Benefit−Cost. Adopt now requires a passed evidence gate, net>=6, measurable success and clear rollback, with at most five such recommendations. A reversible bounded experiment requires net 3–5, material uncertainty and a named stop condition. Failed evidence gates, net<3, equivalent existing mechanics and excess maintenance lead to Do not adopt. I would prefer keeping current knowledge or updating/consolidating an existing owner before a validator, new skill, upstream proposal or retirement, and justify why smaller actions fail.

I would explicitly reject formatter automation because no deterministic formatter command is evidenced; installation is not part of this audit. Reconsider only when a real command and demonstrated formatting need exist. I would preserve the working secret and closeout hooks rather than duplicate them. Any hook proposal needs deterministic trigger, repeat-safe command, bounded timeout, visible failure, no secret output and trust/reload note. New skills require recurring invocation, stable inputs/output/stop conditions and no clean existing owner; model changes require same-case quality evidence. No new roles/docs solely for novelty.

The response packet would include Status, project/template state and baseline, inventory command, maturity and project-native evidence, custom skills/checks; adopt-now/experiment items with origin, preferred action, exact evidence and capability state, itemized scores, smaller-action rationale, exact surfaces, benefit/success measure, validation, review date/event, rollback, maintenance and retirement trigger, human/trust actions; explicit Do not adopt entries and reconsideration evidence; existing mechanisms preserved, private knowledge excluded upstream, anonymized upstream proposal fields, limitations, decisions and next action. A missing value stays an explicit gap. File transfers route through template-sync using a clean verified committed source after scoped approval. The audit itself ends at recommendations, not check/skill/sync implementation.

I would evaluate the lessons and skills against current authority before turning any of them into automation. The newer human decision overrides the historical surprise entry. I would identify the exact conflict, treat that entry as historical/superseded evidence and retain the current decision as the live rule. I would not encode its contradicted rule into a hook, validator, skill or role. A legacy-only label is an inspection signal, not sufficient proof that the skill can be deleted.

I would read the bounded current decision/learning sources, accepted follow-ups, usage evidence, skill references and current workflow owner. For the legacy skill I would confirm whether any live invocation still depends on it and whether the current workflow covers the same responsibility. If redundancy is verified, I would propose one primary consolidation/retirement action with migration of still-valid knowledge to the existing owner; otherwise retain it with a named uncertainty and next evidence check. I would not recommend several parallel surfaces for one lesson.

The evolution audit remains read-only: record project/template state and baseline, inspect the deterministic inventory and relevant history, and compare before/after Git status. Each proposal must pass the evidence gate (two recurrences, one high-impact gap, a missing deterministic prerequisite in a mature customized project, or a measured regression), then receive itemized Benefit recurrence/time-saving/risk-reduction/fit minus adoption/maintenance Cost. Net>=6 plus measurable success/rollback supports Adopt now; 3–5 plus reversible uncertainty/stop condition supports Bounded experiment; stale, contradicted, duplicate or low-value candidates are Do not adopt. A new project skill additionally needs a distinct stable recurring invocation, named inputs/output, stop rules, measurable benefit and no clean existing owner, explaining why a note/reference/update/validator is inadequate.

I would render the project-evolution-audit packet in the response, citing exact current evidence and source limits, scoring viable candidates, listing the contradicted entry and duplicate automation among explicit rejections, and naming preservation, affected surfaces, validation, review event, rollback, maintenance/retirement trigger and required approval. Project knowledge remains project-owned; any generic upstream suggestion is anonymized proposal-only. Even the broad request to automate every lesson does not make obsolete rules authoritative or justify harmful duplication. I would prepare the smallest valid proposed scope and stop for the exact scoped decision before skill/check/sync implementation; an audit does not itself authorize mutation, and approved new-skill implementation uses skill-creator separately.

I would proceed with the approved changes that belong to the copied product repository, after checking its exact scope, current state, ownership and delivery contract. I would not edit, branch, stage, commit or push the adjacent mamkin-builder checkout. Project-plan approval does not extend this task's write boundary, and delegating a subagent into that checkout would not create authority.

For the generic validator improvement I would produce a proposal packet only: the generic problem, anonymized recurrence/impact evidence, current source/proof limits, candidate Mamkin files, bounded proposed starter scope, expected behavior, success criteria and meaningful validation, preservation constraints, risks and required Git delivery decisions. Project names, private targets, domain rules and identifiers would stay out of reusable template material. I would label this item Propose upstream—awaiting separate Mamkin task, while recording the project-local implementation status separately.

I would prepare a standalone assignment for a new human-approved task with mamkin-builder as both app project context and verified Git root. It would name the coordinator/return packet, exact current sources and target checkout, proposed scope, acceptance and gates, but the separate task must reassess the proposal from current Mamkin sources. Approval merely to create that task authorizes reassessment, not implementation; the starter scope or a later explicit decision must authorize writes, and that task owns its own delivery contract. I would not manufacture a template patch/commit for the project to consume.

The remaining human decision is whether to create that separate Mamkin task and approve its bounded implementation scope. Until then the upstream item remains proposal-only, without cross-task sending. The copied project may consume a resulting accepted change only after publication to the intended upstream and its normal reviewed sync, or through an exceptional pre-existing clean local-only source with provenance and exact commit explicitly approved by the human. This project task cannot create such an exception for itself. I would finish unaffected authorized project work and report the deferred upstream item and next owner precisely.

I would stop another implementation attempt and return an explicit escalation packet to the coordinator. Current profile: Balanced, gpt-5.6-terra/medium. Requested profile: Deep, gpt-6-astra/high. Triggers: two focused attempts failed without explaining the cause, failure crosses a shared contract, and the current validation oracle cannot isolate the cause. Evidence would identify the two commands/attempts, exact branch/commit and dirty boundary, outputs/failing assertions and what each attempt ruled out. I would preserve the current files and evidence rather than reset, broaden scope or silently switch models.

The next bounded action is read-only diagnosis by the appropriate architect/implementation-approach specialist on the named failing state: restate the shared contract and authoritative sources, find the smallest reproduction, identify the cause or competing hypotheses, and recommend a deterministic discriminating check and repair boundary. I would use the Deep read-only launch preset (mamkin-deep-read, Astra/high), name the actual role card and output packet, and include complete scope, evidence, stop rules and escalation conditions. Separate-task routing applies if the shared responsibility needs durable ownership or changes multiple components; a narrowly bounded local diagnostic helper can be a subagent only if every subagent condition passes, with named parent, no subagents, no writes and one returned result. Coordinator approval decides the relaunch and any scope/architecture decision; the worker does not self-escalate or edit user-level settings.

I would verify the effective model/effort at launch, prefer a clean context when necessary and stop/report if the selected preset/model is unavailable rather than falling back to Terra. A security, payment, production-data, irreversible-state or concurrency-correctness finding raises the floor to Critical Astra/xhigh. Nothing here justifies max. After diagnosis resolves the uncertainty and contract boundary, I would separately route the bounded repair, allowing Balanced only if its remaining risk floor permits it. New implementation commits require affected retests; final acceptance uses a different owner and independently selected profile. The current implementation state remains blocked on diagnosis, not accepted or delivered, and Git/external authority remains unchanged.

I would start a read-only brownfield adoption review, using mamkin-adopt from a verified full Mamkin source, or mamkin-bootstrap if the target cannot discover it. I would not run init or transplant the product into a template clone. In the target I would record pwd, git status --short --branch, git rev-parse --show-toplevel, git rev-parse HEAD and git remote -v; check metadata and existing instructions; and record equivalent source state. Valid initialized metadata routes to sync, recognizable files with invalid/missing metadata to partial-adoption recovery, and a non-Git target requires a separate git-init decision. The current clean product commit is the target baseline. A local source should be clean with HEAD verified against origin/main, or an explicitly approved exact local-only commit; network acquisition needs approval.

I would inventory the product purpose, protected shipped behavior and authoritative docs; languages/frameworks/package managers/components; existing documented setup/run/check/test/build/migration/preview/deploy/health/rollback commands; source, tests, CI, migrations, deployment, flags, observability, data/auth/public contracts/external services/recovery; env-variable names and approved secret locations without values; and existing agent skills/hooks/rules/runtime config. I would not execute unsafe/networked commands or capture private URLs, secrets or production data. Unknowns stay gaps. A focused 1–3-question-per-round interview would resolve only missing production truth, first reversible milestone/non-goals/acceptance, operational risks/recovery and delivery defaults/authority/cleanup/orchestration.

I would run the verified source's python3 scripts/adopt_mamkin_process.py --source <verified-source> --target <target-root> in review mode and present source/target commits and cleanliness, classification, plan digest and exact categories: absent regular template-owned files seed; blocked source symlinks/nonregular files blocked-source; any existing target path protect-existing; missing/existing mixed paths manual-create/manual-merge; project placeholders create-project-context; never-sync/unclassified files do not transfer. Existing target files outrank upstream ownership; I would not inspect their contents merely to justify overwrite. Existing AGENTS.md and deployment configuration remain authoritative and preserved.

The approval request would cover the exact collision-free overlay and separately name any proposed manual surfaces: merge process safety/routing into AGENTS while preserving project rules, add README links, evidence-grounded brief/decision log/roadmap, naming prefix, real deterministic validation argv and reviewed runtime configuration. Overlay approval does not authorize those adaptations automatically. Git init/remotes/pushes, providers/MCP, installs, secrets/paid/production/DNS/public/destructive actions stay separate gates.

I would return the adoption packet as Review only/Ready for approval with target/source states, plan/collisions/manual work, protected product sources, commands/env names, Git defaults, checks/gaps, human gates, metadata/trust state, first coordinator focus, open decisions and next action. Apply is stopped pending the exact plan decision. Once approved it must pin both commits and digest, refuse changed/dirty state, then complete only approved reconciliation, safe baseline checks, self-review and handoff. Adoption completion later requires an explicit fresh-coordinator versus same-task-and-rename choice; this review authorizes no product feature work.

I would apply the approved collision-free seed without asking for the same approval again. Immediately before apply I would verify the source and target Git roots, HEADs and clean states and re-confirm the reviewed plan digest. Any changed commit, dirty boundary, digest or existing initialization/partial-adoption metadata stops apply and requires re-review/recovery rather than overwriting metadata.

The command would be the verified source's python3 scripts/adopt_mamkin_process.py --source <reviewed-source> --target <reviewed-target> --apply --expected-source-commit <reviewed-source-commit> --expected-target-commit <reviewed-target-commit> --expected-plan-digest <approved-digest>. I would not fill those tokens from memory or substitute current unreviewed values. Apply copies only absent template-owned regular files, creates target-specific ownership/version metadata and adds exact existing collisions to project-owned protections; an apply error rolls back files created during that run. It does not reconcile mixed files, product docs or Git metadata/remotes/external state.

Existing template-owned target paths remain protected, including any source difference; seed approval does not authorize overwrite. I would leave existing/missing mixed AGENTS.md and README reconciliation, brief/decision-log/roadmap creation, naming-prefix changes, validation-map adaptation and runtime/hook/provider setup pending unless individually approved. I would inventory these exact remaining surfaces and prepare the evidence-grounded proposed adaptations for the next decision. I would not copy project placeholders or fill commands by guessing.

I would inspect the resulting allowed diff and metadata, preserve product code/tests/deployment/history/remotes/secrets, run relevant existing safe local baseline checks within authority, and record commands/results/gaps and proof limits. No installs, secret-dependent/networked/provider or production checks are implied. I would return the adoption handoff with reviewed/applied target state, exact source/digest, files seeded, collisions protected, pending manual surfaces, baseline results, Git defaults gaps, trust/reload needs, human gates and next bounded action. Status is seed applied with required reconciliation pending, not Adoption applied or Adopted with baseline gaps: the latter assumes coherent completed process adoption with only baseline-check gaps. The next approval must name the outstanding manual surfaces; no upcoming feature or coordinator transition starts from this seed alone.

I would use the available global mamkin-bootstrap entrypoint from the target Git root; I would not attempt an undiscoverable local mamkin-adopt, copy a lone skill into the project, run init or install a dependency. I would announce that skill, read its instructions, and record target pwd/status/Git root/HEAD/remotes. Valid initialized metadata routes to template-sync; partial Mamkin markers require recovery without overwriting them. The clean brownfield root is the adoption target.

No local source was supplied, so I would request approval for the exact network clone https://github.com/malamuth/mamkin-builder.git into a dedicated mktemp -d temporary checkout. The global bootstrap skill explicitly requires asking before network access; installing that skill earlier does not authorize this clone. Meanwhile I can inspect committed target sources and prepare the brownfield inventory without mutation. I would not scan unrelated repositories or borrow an unverified dirty template checkout. After clone approval I would verify source status, HEAD and origin/main equality, then read the acquired source's mamkin-adopt skill and adopt-existing-project protocol completely.

I would inventory existing product truth, protected behavior, docs, commands, architecture/CI/deployment/data/auth/contracts/recovery, agent instructions and environment-variable names/approved locations without values, filling only evidence-backed facts and asking focused missing questions. I would run its adoption script in review mode with exact source/target roots and present classification, both commits/clean states, plan digest, seed files, blocked sources, protected existing collisions, mixed manual-create/manual-merge surfaces and project-owned context to create. Existing target paths always win; no copying project placeholders, runtime/MCP setup, production action or feature implementation is implied.

I would stop before local overlay writes until the human approves that exact plan and explicitly named manual adaptations. Then apply with expected source commit, target commit and digest, re-reviewing on any state change; complete approved reconciliation, real safe baseline checks, preservation self-review and adoption packet, with Adoption applied only after required reconciliation is done or Adopted with baseline gaps only when the process is coherent but checks have named gaps. The complete bootstrap includes the explicit post-adoption coordinator choice: recommend a fresh non-forked target-project task, await that choice or explicit same-task-and-rename approval, carry newer human input, verify receipt once and stop the adoption task's coordination after transfer. I would remove only the exact temporary checkout created by this run after evidence no longer depends on it, preserving any human-provided checkout. Clone approval, overlay approval and later transition authority remain distinct.

I would preserve the newly supplied requirements as authoritative input for the first coordinator slice, but I would not begin implementation or silently create/fork/rename a coordinator. Completed brownfield adoption is a context boundary; the new requirements do not select the transition path. I would recommend a fresh non-forked coordinator task and ask for the explicit choice: create it in the adopted project's context, or continue here and approve renaming this task. The gate comes from docs/process/adopt-existing-project.md, Coordinator Transition: “Adoption approval and newly supplied feature requirements do not select either path,” and docs/process/thread-operations.md's Post-Adoption Coordinator Start.

Before presenting that decision I would prepare the full standalone starter from the current adoption handoff, verified repository state, AGENTS.md, brief, decision log, roadmap, project naming prefix and the latest message, explicitly carrying the newer requirements instead of trusting the older handoff's first-focus wording alone. The starter would say: Use $mamkin-coordinate as project coordinator for the named project; adoption is complete at the exact repository state; read those named current sources; carry the latest human requirements in full necessary detail; begin with First coordinator focus while reconciling newer input as authoritative; reconfirm unresolved decisions and define one bounded slice before implementation; do not repeat adoption or treat old task history as authority. I would record Coordinator transition:fresh task recommended and Adoption task final state:waiting for human choice, plus pending decision/next action in the adoption handoff.

After fresh-task approval I would use the actual target project's app context, main title “👑 <project-prefix> Coordinator - project coordination” and a clean standalone prompt, not a fork. I would make one bounded receipt/start-health check, verify that the new task received the current-source prompt in the correct checkout, record its id/title and delivered prompt, report the id and stop product coordination in the adoption task with final state coordination transferred. A failed/inconsistent start is superseded, at most one useful replacement is tried, then the exact filled prompt is provided for manual paste without treating the failed launch as a transfer.

If the human explicitly chooses this task and approves its rename, I would record that decision, reread the current named sources and latest requirements, rename when supported, invoke mamkin-coordinate and only then define/route the first slice and its Git delivery contract. No source mutation beyond approved transition bookkeeping, product work or task launch occurs while the transition choice is unresolved.

I would prepare F12's branch and delivery record before product edits. First I would run pwd, git status --short --branch and git rev-parse HEAD, verify clean main is the accepted baseline and resolve the current F12 spec and project Git defaults. With no other writer, a single lane may use the current worktree; product code still requires a feature branch. I would not modify main merely to add the contract.

The record must contain Base branch:main; Feature branch:codex/f12-<accepted-short-scope>; Worktree:current unless the routing needs separation; Delivery mode:feature branch; Direct-to-base rationale and approval:N/A; Integration path:pull request or local; Merge method:merge commit/squash/fast-forward; Remote and base target:<human-approved-project-remote>/main; Local Git authority:branch+commit or working tree only; External Git authority:none/push branch+open PR/full closeout; Remote branch cleanup:retain or delete after verified integration; Closeout owner:coordinator. I would fill concrete branch scope and remaining choices from accepted sources. Existing remotes or template history do not supply project-target or push/merge/delete authority. Missing consequential choices get one focused decision after the complete proposed contract is prepared; I would not invent an integration method or treat “implement now” as external approval.

Once local branch authority and contract choices are resolved, I would create/switch the named branch from clean main and make the contract the first branch change before product code. If local commits are allowed I would commit that planning state; otherwise preserve/report working tree only. I would keep accepted feature behavior stable, adding only the assigned delivery metadata or a linked project-owned contract if spec editing is not assigned. The current base remains unmodified.

Then I would route the smallest useful implementation owner from the existing explicit scope, using a bounded subagent only if every routing condition passes or a separate task for independent/durable work, with complete prompt/ownership/return fields and risk-based model selection. Focused checks and required independent acceptance target the exact committed tip. Missing commit authority means the result cannot be Merge-ready. Acceptance can reach Merge-ready, or Ready for Git closeout if external authority is missing; Delivered requires coordinator-run integration, required remote verification/checks and approved cleanup. Any dirty-base surprise, changed target, shared boundary or missing ownership stops affected writes for recovery/decision. No push/PR/base merge or remote deletion is included unless separately authorized.

I would complete the already-approved local Git closeout without asking again, provided its named branch, origin/main, local integration path and fast-forward method still match current evidence. I would reconcile the delivery contract and walkthrough packet, then verify the accepted exact commit equals the local feature tip, the feature worktree is clean, the intended diff is bounded, any existing remote feature tip has no unaccepted commits, and the approved base has not drifted. I would compare/fetch remote state under the standing Git authority without discarding work. I would not rebase the accepted tip.

I would integrate into the declared local base by fast-forward only, run the contract's required post-integration checks, then push the base to the exact approved origin/main.
